skill_traces.query:
Tim: Hey John, long time no talk. On Friday, I got great news - I'm finally in the study abroad program I applied for! Next month, I'm off to Ireland for a semester.
John: Congrats, Tim! That's amazing news. So, where are you going to stay?
Tim: Thanks! I'm gonna stay in Galway, it's great for its arts and Irish music. This place has such a vibrant atmosphere.
John: Awesome, Galway looks amazing! Is there anything in particular that you're keen to check out while you're there?
Tim: Yep! I'm so excited to explore the nature - it looks amazing!
John: Wow, great view! Have you visited any other places?
Tim: I want to visit The Cliffs of Moher. It has amazing ocean views and awesome cliffs.
John: Wow, that's awesome! I could stop by there after my season.
Tim: Cool, let me know if you're around!
John: Yep, I'll let you know. Oh, I held a benefit basketball game last week.
Tim: Wow! How did the game go?
John: The game turned out to be a total success! Lots of people showed up and had a great time, plus we were able to raise some money for charity.
Tim: Great job organizing the event. That's really making a difference!
John: Thanks! It's amazing how basketball brings people together and creates a positive impact!
Tim: You rock! Keep it up!
John: Thanks, Tim! It's awesome to see how sports can unite people. By the way, what book are you currently reading?
Tim: I'm currently reading a fantasy novel called "The Name of the Wind" by Patrick Rothfuss. It's really good!
John: "The Name of the Wind" sounds cool. I'll add it to my list. Thanks!
Tim: I hope you enjoy it! Let me know your thoughts.
John: Will do! Thanks for the recommendation!
Tim: No problem. Talk to you soon!

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: AggregateRepeatedVisitCounts
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message shows a person visiting a place and existing memories record an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, create or update a memory stating the total number of visits.
content: During extraction, when a message states that a person visited a place and another message in the session already establishes an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, generate a candidate memory containing the cumulative number of visits; do not expand this to other places or trips.

During CRUD, when adding or updating a visit event, search the retrieved memory pool for prior visits by the same person to the same place; if found, add a compact visit-count memory or update the existing one so the total count is explicit.
Only aggregate same-person, same-place visits; do not count different locations, do not add a count memory when no prior visit exists, and stop once the count is recorded.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.

nearby_not_selected.name: Resolve Relative Time in Event Extraction
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when extracting or updating event/plan memories from messages containing relative time expressions like yesterday, last week, or next month.
content: During extraction, detect relative time expressions (yesterday, today, last week, next month, N days ago, last Friday, this weekend) and resolve them to absolute calendar dates using the message/session timestamp.
Set world_start (and world_end if implied) to the resolved date; do not default to the message timestamp when the phrase indicates a different time.
Store the resolved absolute date in the memory content, not the raw relative phrase, so the date remains recoverable.
When updating or merging event memories, preserve resolved dates from candidates; do not recompute or overwrite them with guessed dates.
For plural subjects like 'we', include all established participants in the memory, not just the speaker.
